sentences.text: The vs Judge

on 21 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No.2835 of 2012
Judgment:

The appellant is the Claimant in M.V.O.P.No.1011 of 2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- Principal District Judge, Vizianagaram and the respondents are the respondents in the said case.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal -cum- Principal District Judge, Vizianagaram
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed in the claim application.

3. The claimant filed a Claim Petition under section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the respondents praying the Tribunal to award an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a Motor Vehicle Accident occurred on 10.11.2009.
4.

The brief averments of the petition are as follows:
On 10.11.2009 the petitioner went to NRI hospital, Sagivalasa to hand over carriage to his wife, while returning, he boarded an auto bearing No.AP 31X 3651, when the auto reached Timber 2 VGKRJ MACMA 2835 of 2012 Depot, Tagarapuvalasa, the driver of auto bearing No.AP 35T 5612 coming in opposite direction, drove the auto in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the auto in which the petitioner was travelling, resulting which the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and the petitioner claimed an amount of Rs.3,00,000/- towards compensation.
5. The first respondent remained exparte.

The second respondent filed counter denying the claim of claimant and contended that there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner and the petitioner is not entitled any compensation and the second respondent is not liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

6. Based on the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues:
i. Whether the accident was occurred resulting injuries caused to the petitioner, due to rash and negligent driving of the vehicle auto bearing No.AP 35T 5612 by its driver 1st respondent?
3 VGKRJ MACMA 2835 of 2012 ii. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, at what quantum and what is the liability of respondents?

iii. To what relief?

1 7.
During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, PW1 and PW2 were examined and Ex.A1 to Ex.
A8 and
Ex .X1 and Ex.X2 were marked.
No oral evidence was adduced on behalf of respondents, however Ex.B1 was marked.

8. At the culmination of the enquiry, after considering the evidence on record and on appreciation of the same, the Tribunal has given a finding that there is a negligence on the part of the first respondent in driving his auto and there is also contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner,
but not on the part of the driver of the auto in which the petitioner was travelling and the Tribunal granted an amount of Rs.92,316/- to the claimant towards compensation, since there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
9. Aggrieved by the same, the claimant filed the present appeal claiming the remaining balance of compensation amount.
4 VGKRJ MACMA 2835 of 2012 10.

Now, the points for consideration are:
1. Whether the Order of Tribunal needs any interference?
2. Whether the claimant/ appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as prayed for?
11. POINT Nos.1 and 2:-
On appreciation of the entire evidence on record and on considering Ex.A1 attested copy of First Information Report and Ex.A3 true copy of charge sheet, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also due to negligence on the part of the claimant because the claimant sat by the side of the driver of the auto and opposite auto touched the legs of the claimant.

On appreciation of the entire evidence on record, the Tribunal arrived that there is contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner and 50% of the amount was deducted from out of the total compensation awarded to the claimant.

12. The material on record clearly reveals that the accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the 5 VGKRJ MACMA 2835 of 2012 driving of the offending auto and there was also a negligence on the part of the petitioner, who is travelling in the auto by sitting by side of the auto driver.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly came to conclusion that there was a contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.

13. Coming to the compensation, the Tribunal awarded total compensation of Rs.1,84,632/-, from out of which 50% of amount was deducted towards contributory negligent on the part of the The vs Judge on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90356835/
2 petitioner and an amount of Rs.92,316/- only was awarded to the claimant towards compensation.
The Tribunal, on appreciation of the entire evidence on record, came to conclusion that the petitioner sustained two grievous injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident.
The evidence of PW2/Dr.K.V.Muralimohan, who treated the petitioner coupled with Ex.A2 wound certificate proves that the petitioner sustained two grievous injuries in a Motor Vehicle Accident.
Therefore, the compensation of Rs.50,000/- granted by the Tribunal towards two grievous injuries is enhanced to Rs.60,000/- @ Rs.30,000/- each.

The Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.5,000/-
6 VGKRJ MACMA 2835 of 2012 towards special diet and extranourishment and on considering the Ex.A6 bunch of medical bills an amount of Rs.7,232/- was awarded to the petitioner towards medical bills.
I do not find any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding given by the Tribunal in granting compensation under the two above heads.
14. The evidence of PW2 coupled with Ex.X1 case sheet and Ex.A7 disability certificate clearly proves that the petitioner is suffering with a disability of 40%.
By giving cogent reasons, the Tribunal came to conclusion that the claimant is suffering from 20% disability.
It is a settled law that a disability to a particular limb cannot be considered as a disability to whole body.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly held that the petitioner is suffering from disability of 20%.
The monthly income of the injured was arrived at Rs.3,000/- per month i.e., Rs.36,000/- per annum.
The age of the petitioner is 25 years.
The multiplier applicable to the age group of the petitioner is 18.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.1,29,600/- (36,000 x 20% x 18) is awarded towards 20% disability.

The petitioner was admitted in the hospital as inpatient and he was in the hospital for a period of 45 days, therefore, an amount of Rs.6,000/- is awarded towards loss of 7 VGKRJ MACMA 2835 of 2012 earnings during the period of treatment.
The material on record reveals that the petitioner sustained three simple injuries.
Therefore, an amount of Rs.3,000/- is awarded towards each simple injury.
In total an amount of Rs.9,000/- is awarded towards three simple injuries.
An amount of Rs.5,000/- is awarded towards transportation charges.
In total, the claimant is entitled an amount of Rs.2,21,832/-.

Accordingly,
the claim amount of Rs.1,84,632/- granted by the Tribunal is enhanced to Rs.2,21,832/-.
From out of which 50% has to be deducted towards contributory negligence on the part of the petitioner.
Accordingly the petitioner is entitled an amount of Rs.1,10,916/- (2,21,832 / 2) towards compensation.

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled an amount of Rs.18,600/- (1,10,916 - 92,316)
towards enhanced compensation.
It is the case of both sides that there are no violations in Ex.B1 policy and the driver of the offending vehicle is having valid driving licence by the date of accident.

15. In the result, this appeal is partly allowed, modifying the order dated 02.05.2012 passed in MVOP No.1011/2010 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Vizianagaram and the claim amount is enhanced from Rs.92,316/-
8 VGKRJ MACMA 2835 of 2012 to Rs.1,10,916/-.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner is entitled the enhanced compensation of Rs.18,600/- with interest @6% p.a. from the date of petition, till the date of realization.
The respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the enhanced compensation with interest as ordered above, before the Tribunal within two months from the date of this judgment.
On such deposit, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw the same along with accrued interest thereon.
There shall be no order as to costs.
